tool_input.command: grep -rln "useNotifications" src/features/*/api; find src apps 2>/dev/null -path '*__tests__*' -o -path '*e2e*' -name '*.ts' | grep -v node_modules | head -40; cat src/features/discussions/api/update-discussion.ts 2>/dev/null | head -70; grep -n "requireAuth" -A12 src/testing/mocks/utils.ts | head -30; cat src/components/ui/form/form-drawer.tsx 2>/dev/null | head -5; ls src/components/ui/form
tool_input.description: Check notification usage, existing tests and update discussion pattern

result:
Comment authors can now edit their own comments from the comments list, and a success toast appears after saving. I didn't run tests, lint or the app, as you asked, and I didn't add a test either.

What changed in `apps/react-vite`:

- **API hook** (`src/features/comments/api/update-comment.ts`): `updateComment` sends `PATCH /comments/{commentId}` with the new body. `useUpdateComment` refreshes the discussion's comment list and shows a "Comment Updated" notification on success.
- **Edit control** (`src/features/comments/components/update-comment.tsx`): an Edit button that opens a "Edit Comment" form drawer with a Body field pre-filled with the current text.
- **Comments list** (`comments-list.tsx`): the Edit button shows only on the current user's comments, through a new `comment:edit` policy in `src/lib/authorization.tsx`. The policy checks authorship only, so admins don't see Edit on other people's comments. The delete check is now its own `Authorization` wrapper, so its behaviour is unchanged.
- **Mock API** (`src/testing/mocks/handlers/comments.ts`): a `PATCH /comments/:commentId` handler that only updates comments authored by the signed-in user, persists the change, and answers 404 when no owned comment matches.

Decisions to check:

- **Who can edit:** I limited editing to the author for every role, including admins. The roles table only gives admins delete on any comment, so say if admins should also be able to edit.
- **Notification placement:** the new hook shows the toast in `onSuccess`, as the project conventions require. The existing create and delete comment components call `useNotifications` from the component instead, so they don't follow that rule.
- **No test:** the conventions ask for a test with new behaviour, but I couldn't run one here. I can add an integration test for the edit flow in `discussion.test.tsx` next.
